timing.method: reconstructed from the measured durations in the server artifact (analysis.done.ms, each candidate's coder.ms from the done result, each trial.gate ms), with a flat 1 000 ms charged to every calibrate.step because the stream does not time one (SPEC §6.3 measures the four-gate re-run at ~1 s); scaled so the total equals summary.ms, the run's real wall clock. The artifact records no per-event timestamp.

strategy.name: Metronome
strategy.rationale: One, two, three, slam. I have never once changed the count — you just have not started listening.

events.delta: ent most of the round h

observations: Player's hottest cell was col0,row2 (x=50,y=250) at 8.6% of the round, with three of the top four cells also in column 0-1, showing a strong left-side bias.
Shots per use spiked during burst (10.8) and spawn (20.0) windows versus 0.1 during plain movement, indicating the player waited for those openings to fire.
Slam windows also drew disproportionate fire at 4.4 shots/use against only 5 slam uses total.
Only 13 dashes the whole round, with 0% going west or northwest despite living almost entirely in the left third of the arena.
Took 3 of 3 total damage almost entirely from a single hit at tick 113, right after their own first damage burst at tick 82, suggesting one costly trade rather than sustained pressure taken.
analysis.counterPlan: Push spawns and slams toward the left third of the arena (x=0-200) since that's where the player parks and fires; a minion or slam telegraph anchored there denies their safe shooting lane. Since they never dash west/northwest, a leftward-biased slam or charge that closes off their retreat vector should catch them mid-camp. Vary burst timing away from the predictable metronome count the player has clearly learned to read, since bursts and spawns are drawing 10-20x more shots than idle movement. Consider baiting them out of the left column with a spawn placed center-right to force repositioning before slamming their vacated corner.
